title_en: The Night of Power and the sending down of the Quran
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power; the verse does not name what 'it' is.
The verse asks the one addressed what would let him know what the Night of Power is.
The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.
The angels and the Spirit come down in it, by the permission of their Lord, with every matter.
It is peace until the rising of dawn.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power [c1]. The Night of Power is better than a thousand months [c3], and the angels and the Spirit come down in it by the permission of their Lord [c4]. It is peace until the rising of dawn [c5].
chapters.body_md:
God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power; the verse does not name what it is [c1]. The verse then asks the one addressed what would let him know what the Night of Power is [c2].

The Night of Power is better than a thousand months [c3]. The angels and the Spirit come down in it, by the permission of their Lord, with every matter [c4]. It is peace until the rising of dawn [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage answers its own question by saying what the night is better than [c2][c3]. It speaks of a coming down of the angels and the Spirit, and says that it happens by the permission of their Lord [c4]. The last verse describes the night as peace and gives its end as the rising of dawn [c5].
chapters.kids_md: God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power [c1]. This night is better than a thousand months [c3]. The angels and the Spirit come down in it, by the permission of their Lord [c4]. It is peace until the dawn rises [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage invites attention to a single night by saying what it is better than [c3]. Another is that peace is how the passage describes the night [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which night this is, in which month, or how a believer would know it. The verses give none of this.
- Not established: what the thousand months measures, or how a night can be better than that; the verse says only that it is.
- Not established: what 'it' refers to in 97:1. Other chapters of this story speak of the Quran being sent down, and the inventory groups them; this verse does not name it.
- Not established: what 'every matter' includes, or who the Spirit is; the verse names the Spirit beside the angels and says no more here.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the date of the night and the identification of the Spirit. Neither is used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: God swears by the clear Book and says that He sent it down in a blessed night.
God says that He has always been one who warns.
In that night every wise matter is made distinct, as a command from God, who says that He has always been one who sends.
It is a mercy from the Lord of the one addressed, who is the one who hears and knows.

chapters.summary_md: God swears by the clear Book and says that He sent it down in a blessed night [c1]. In it every wise matter is made distinct, as a command from Him [c3]. It is a mercy from the Lord of the one addressed [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God swears by the clear Book and says that He sent it down in a blessed night [c1]. He says that He has always been one who warns [c2].

In that night every wise matter is made distinct, as a command from God, who says that He has always been one who sends [c3]. It is a mercy from the Lord of the one addressed, who is the one who hears and knows [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The night is called blessed [c1], and the passage says that in it every wise matter is made distinct [c3]. The passage ties the sending down to warning [c1][c2] and to a command from God [c3]. It ends by naming the whole as mercy [c4].
chapters.kids_md: God says that He sent it down in a blessed night [c1]. God says that He has always been one who warns [c2]. It is a mercy from our Lord, who hears and knows [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage presents the sending down of the Book as warning and as mercy together [c2][c4]. Another is that it speaks of a night as blessed without describing what happens to it [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: that the blessed night here is the night of power of the previous chapter. The verses do not say so; the inventory and later readers group them.
- Not established: what the letters at the opening of the surah mean, or what 'made distinct' covers.
- Not established: what 'it' is in 44:3 beyond the clear Book that God swears by; whether it is the whole Quran or a part is not said.
- Not established: when the blessed night was or in what month.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of this night with the night of power. It is not used in the story texts.

chapters.title_en: The month of the sending down

claims.statement_en: The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Quran was sent down, as guidance for the people and as clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion.
God says that He wants ease for them and does not want hardship for them.
The verse gives as aims that they complete the period, that they magnify God for having guided them, and that they give thanks.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran was sent down in the month of Ramadan, as guidance for the people and as clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion [c1]. God says that He wants ease for them and not hardship [c2].
chapters.body_md:
The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Quran was sent down, as guidance for the people and as clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion [c1].

The verse says that God wants ease for them and does not want hardship for them [c2]. It gives as aims that they complete the period, that they magnify God for having guided them, and that they give thanks [c3].
chapters.deep_md: This verse names the month in which the sending down took place [c1]. It describes the Quran by the words guidance, clear proofs of the guidance, and the criterion [c1]. It links the month to ease and to gratitude [c2][c3].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran was sent down in the month of Ramadan [c1]. It is guidance for the people [c1]. God says that He wants ease for us and not hardship [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the verse joins the sending down of the Quran to thanks for having been guided [c1][c3]. Another is that it states ease as God's wish [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the night of the month in which the sending down took place, or whether the sending down here is the same event as in the other chapters; the verse says only that the Quran was sent down in the month.
- Not established: whether 'sent down' here means all at once or in parts. Another story speaks of parts.
- The verse goes on to speak about fasting in this month and about those who are sick or travelling. Those provisions are not restated here; this draft gives no judgement on them, and a scholar should decide whether and how the page presents them.
- The Arabic word translated 'the criterion' (furqan) is read in more than one way and is left as a rendering for the reviewer.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the Night of Power, on the sending down of the Quran in the month, and on the date of the night, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

The chapters rest on separate passages. The verses do not say in so many words that the blessed night, the Night of Power and the month are one event; the inventory groups them, and a scholar should decide how the page states the link.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the date of the Night of Power and the identification of the Spirit named in the passage.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
